english: He's looking for some genuine shit here.
Don't be too human-negative. He won't like that.
Follow what your heart is whispering.
Exasperation.
Breathless thinking.
There is a good answer.
Be straight with him.
This is the kind of moment where you make sure to remember: Urth was just a guy.
And now, you're the ones left to pick up the pieces.
He was just a man. A man endowed by divine spark. Treat him like any other human, and you will see the truth.
Remember what he told you. His Era is over. You and I are the ones here. This is our city now.
He shouldn't have gone to Askan to begin with.
I don't know, Snell. I'm only human.
The goblin looks up.
Alright. I can do that.
You would make an excellent leader of the Halfways.
You said it yourself, everything changes after the election. It's a new world now.
Urth is dead. We are alive. That is all that matters.
Your comment forces him to a short laugh.
I don't think anyone could live up to Sageleaf, if she ever croaks.
But thanks.
Guess I did.
Guess it is.
Maybe it is. Maybe you're right.
He should have let us all drown.
He should have gambled on some other plan. No matter the odds.
We all should have died in the old country, by man-made cursebombs and magically infused legionnaire blades.
Maybe he should've.
But if I were in his shoes, I'd probably have done the same thing.
If I had to choose between the Halfways making it, or the rest of you humans, that is.
You'd defend a handful of goblins over, the lives of way more humans?
I would also choose that. I hate humans now.
As would I. For humans.
He shrugs. "Depends on the exact amount, I guess. But..."
Maybe. Yeah.
Your comment forces a laugh out of him.
Sure you do.
I'm sure you would.
The goblin's eyes are full of contemplation.
He will think about this conversation as much as he will about the one with your god.
Couldn't have gone better.
A String is woven. The path is set.
Feel the warmth and strands and calming frays.
He's not so bad, after everything.
A goblin with good spirit might be exactly what this city needs.
His tiny mind catches up quicker than you anticipated.
In time he will understand it. He might seek more knowledge from you then.
That quick smile on his face. Yeah.
You did good. No fumbles here.
A goblin. Not a human.
You cannot get too close.
You cannot understand him.
It is too far removed, his position, his life, his skin, his claws and fangs.
Despite this time you have spent together, there is little else to be done.
Was he... not your brother-in-arms?
Did he not watch your back on this dire journey?
That's fair. I never liked him that much anyhow. (Let the moment pass.)
What? That's it?
He was. He was, and has been, my brother-in-arms.
A sad thought. But true.
Then SPEAK.
Seek into his mind.
A man can only bring himself to true power via the bulging arms of his peers.
Let them LIFT you UP.
Become a man, who is NOT an island.
UNDERSTAND HIM.
Understand your brother, despite the world.
Yes?
I really enjoyed hanging out with this little bastard.
I thought he was cool enough.
I didn't have anything against him. Not really.
I wish I got to know him more.
Oh? You did?
Yeah.
I did it!
The dwarf at the front of the queue yells, his voice echoing out into the now almost empty temple chamber.
I finally voted. I actually did it! Hah! He steps back from the ballot box, wiping sweat from his brow.
The dwarf turns to look out over the chamber, tears streaming from his bloodshot eyes.
I didn't think it would be so <shake>difficult</shake>...!
At least you've got one guy who cares as much about politics as you.
Wow. What a, uh... true democracy enjoyer right there.
With this gentleman done, you see nothing now- nothing standing between you and your voice.
Here we go! Time to modernize this fucking place.
Save your city. NOW.
Such a waste of time.
<shake>Rumblings...</shake>
A vote. A trove. A war.
This is the first, in the Rule-of-Three.
E-It's time.
You approach the ballot box.
Its slit: a canyon of possibilities.
You should really try to find a girlfriend.
Time to cast this damn vote.
The guy next to you drops in his own voting card.
As he too leaves the chamber- only you and Snell remain.
Speaking of which. Here.
From his breast pocket, the goblin shows you a freshly printed voting card.
Without any of the boxes filled in.
That is how you vote in the election.
You need one of these if you're planning on voting, you know.
I was supposed to have one?
Oh shit. I'd completely forgotten about that.
Obviously. I know that.
Yeah. Especially if you're a human.
Especially-especially if you're a cleric.
Maybe they forgot to give me one.
Maybe they didn't want me to vote.
Maybe I don't deserve to vote.
You're overthinking it.
...Probably.
Not surprising. Considering the fifty thousand esoteric-bullshit-events we've been through.
A little piece of paper would slip your mind, eh?
Yeah, yeah.
Just take it.
(Look at the voting card.)
Snagged one of these on the way in. You'll need it, after that ballsy move downstairs.
Oh, right. The Living Library...
Yeah. Sorry again about that.
That was almost entirely on me.
I'd completely forgotten about that.
It kind of was, wasn't it? (Smirk.)
Don't worry about it. Shit happens.
(Hold up the voting card.) "We're even now."
Not surprising. Considering the fifty thousand other entirely different esoteric-bullshit-events we've been through.
Don't push it.
A lot of shit happens in dungeons, yeah.
Sounds good to me.
Snagged one of these on the way in. You lost yours, right?
Oh, yeah. I gave it up in the living library.
The what?
...I'll explain later. It was a whole thing. (Look at the new card.)
You rummage in your pouch for a moment, until you find it: your old voting card.
It's so damn crinkled. And all the boxes are filled in for some reason.
I already have one.
Yeah, but they won't accept that.
The rules clearly state, only one box can be filled in.
What does 'filled in' mean in this case?
So I'm only allowed to fill in... one choice.
I'll use yours, then.
(Look at the new card.)
...I'm not entirely sure.
But my guess is it means some type of ink, graphite, or really any type of clear pencil marking.
That's how it works, yeah.
I heard some cities do it with some type of weird ranking system.
But I'm assuming it never caught on, simply because it's way too complicated for the average voter.
...Even more so for the below average voter.
I'm a below average voter, aren't I?
I'm an average voter. Perfectly normal.
I'm above average, obviously.
I don't think I would describe you as that, no.
For multiple complicated reasons.
Something about that description doesn't quite fit you.
Obviously.
Obviously.
Obviously.
Do that.
Noticed that you lost your voting card at some point. Snagged this on the way in.
Oh right. I gave it to the Living Library.
The what now?
You know Snurre Appledent? I found the famous book he was looking for in a Living Library below. I traded it for my voting card.
How did you trade a voting card for a famous book?
Honestly, I thought I couldn't get another voting card.
I guess belief is everything.
(Look at the card.)
You see the Norvikian stamp in the corner.
The Perch. It is official.
The printing is a bit different from the card you received in the mail last week.
Seems like the goblins must have ordered a new batch.
Must be some goblin special version of the voting cards. How lovely.
Thanks.
You always think of everything, don't you?
You've done well, my goblin sidekick.
I never asked for you to get me a card.
Don't mention it.
Oh yeah. I got an eye for detail.
Fuck you.
Yet you still need it. How peculiar.
He holds up another card, looking just as fresh.
I just snagged an extra when I took one for myself.
Unceremoniously, Snell then drops his own voting card into the box.
Huh?
Done.
Oh shit!
This goblin- quick and democratic. What a combo!
He... did it? Just like that?
A power-move.
THE VOTE HAS BEEN CAST.
What? Just like that?!
(Stare at his calm demeanor and gasp.)
What do you want? A fucking ritual? Song and dance?
It's in the box. That's what matters.
He has known for a long time what to put in this box.
I guess I just expected you to care a bit more.
I guess it's not that hard to vote after all.
(Nod.) "Good on you for voting, Snell."
I think I'm just nervous since... this means... (Realize what's happening.)
I've done enough for this election. Half of the Halfways wouldn't even be able to vote if I hadn't gotten those extra papers printed up.
Trust me, I care. But I'm also very happy that it's over.
Eh. Depends on the person, I assume.
Anyhow...
I wasn't gonna not, after all of this.
Snell steps aside.
Your turn, Cleric.
The ballot box looms.
Its shadow: ominous. Emanating an uncertain future.
A fray of NO RETURN.
Good luck with this, Cleric.
He looks around.
There's a few errands I'll need to run before the sun goes down.
So I'll leave you to it.
Turning to leave, he instead looks back with a scrunched expression.
...Just gotta ask one more thing.
The prayer.
The prayer. The old man mentioned you would pray every night for one thing.
It's been killing me, so I gotta ask.
What was it?
Your heart falls onto the floor.
It <shake>meshes</shake> with the dwarven tiles.
Uh.
The goblin gives you an almost desperate look. He needs to hear this.
Eh. Can't hurt to share.
Not like anyone will ever ask you again.
Your most closely guarded secret. Only shared with your god.
Does he deserve to hear it?
It is an idiotic thing.
He will surely enjoy hearing it.
It's a bit private.
I'd prefer to keep that between me and my god.
No, Snell.
It's, uh... (Say it.)
Oh, come on.
You've asked so many questions. Give me an answer for once.
(Laugh nervously.) "Maybe some other day, buddy."
Alright, alright. I get it.
Snell crosses his arms.
I would look out the window each night. I'd look at the, uh, moon and the dark sky. Then I would ask Urth to give me one thing.
He leans in.
(Hold up a finger.)
One. Only one is enough.
I prayed for one friend.
The goblin listens.
One friend. That would be enough.
I was a lonely kid.
Bit sad, isn't it?
That's...
He gives you a shrug.
That's not unreasonable.
It's really not. (Laugh.)
Do I have low standards?
(Just laugh.)
Your goblin companion laughs alongside you.
Potentially, the goblin says, attempting to contain a laugh, "but that's not a bad trait."
He scoffs and gives you a confounding glance.
He holds out a sharp claw.
A handshake.
A show of... friendship.
A brotherhood.
A friendly gesture. Take it.
A hand to shake.
Be careful. Don't touch him too much.
Be cool! Give him a tap or something.
Tickle it.
(Stare at it.)
(Shake it. Firmly.)
(Shake it. Loosely.)
(Tap it.)
(Tickle his palm.)
He gestures to his claw.
Fuck off.
Come on.
I've been patient enough, haven't I?
You give him a firm handshake.
He grins.
You give him a loose handshake.
He gives you a confused laugh.
That's the worst handshake I've ever-
He laughs. "Exactly what I expected."
The goblin meets it with a satisfying slap.
Hells yeah.
He quickly pulls back.
You awkward motherfucker.
Then he laughs.
Your BROTHER-IN-ARMS.
He is going to miss this.
For whatever reason.
See you around, Cleric.
Your goblin companion then walks down the stairs, heading straight for the exit.
You will see him AGAIN.
For your Strings are... INTERLINKED.
As he goes, you hear him yell out, "<shake>And don't vote for anything stupid</shake>!"
(Watch him leave the Temple of Urth.)
Then you're alone.
(Turn back to the ballot box.)
You see it staring at you.
Next to it: a simple pencil.
ALONE.
Just you, and this amazing little box.
Could you imagine? A dozen revolutions. Decades of violence and upheaval- all to get you the chance to write whatever you want on that little piece of paper and drop it in this silly box.
Years of strife, for what?
For your ancestral home to be broken into squabbling pieces.
All for this dream of democracy. A foreign dream.
You are now about to contribute as one-in-approximately-three-hundred-thousand.
For comparison: the textbook on esoteric history you read for your Towers initialization was three-hundred-and-twenty-thousand words long. Imagine yourself as one of those words.
Then realize how vastly little this action matters, in the grand scheme of Norvik.
Yet one singular word in that tome can change its entire meaning.
Vote. Vote for every person, each creature, all things in this world of yours.
You do not know much. But you know... this matters.
Vote.
(Pick up the pencil. Look at the card.)
Everything upon your shoulders.
As you bring forth the voting card - the pencil in your hand - a world watching.
I'm still not sure what to vote.
I know exactly what to vote.
I hope I'm making the right decision.
The ballot box offers no advice.
Yet you must do it.
The ballot box believes you.
So do it.
The ballot box offers no support.
Choose now. One final time.
Is this the VOTING?
Sounds important. Meek thinks master will choose good!
Thanks, Meek.
You wanna help me choose?
<wiggle>Yes</wiggle>! Big thanks to me!
Oh!
Is there mimic to vote for?
There should be. But no.
Then Meek will skip.
A vote is cast for the self.
That is the natural state of things.
Your talking scarf morphs back into a not-talking scarf.
The ballot box calls to you.
You can delay it no longer.
It's just one vote. It doesn't really matter. Right?
What if I choose wrong?
I wonder what will happen to Norvik.
R-I'm going to vote for...
It's more about the symbolism. You know, supporting the democratic revolution, and so on.
That's... actually true. Yeah.
One man fighting against impossible odds.
There is nothing more significant.
Nothing you do really matters. So...
Tense, yet... still.
You are in control here. Make a decision.
Stress. STRESS.
You must <shake>perform</shake>.
There is a reason goodness is aligned with intent, rather than outcome.
If you truly value the world, then there is no wrong choice.
Only an attempt to fight for the right.
No one's ever going to find out what you write on that card of yours. Not really.
If someone asks later, you can just lie.
So don't think too much into it.
There is no correct vote, no wrong one either.
Simply make do with this one singular voice of yours. An insignificant duty in a sea of mediocrity.
Gods be damned, you cannot wait for this election to be over.
Impossible.
That means: not possible.
Difficult to say. Chaos. Order breaking down. Complete collapse.
Or, more logically, nothing at all. Since nothing ever really changes from banalities like democracy.
The city will live on.
It has dealt with bigger issues in the past, and it will survive worse disasters in the future.
You will make sure of it.
Who knows? Maybe it will fall to ruin. Like every other civilization which has inhabited this place previously...
There will be good days ahead.
For you, and all folk of this wonderful city.
Now vote already!
It is still in your Pouch of Holding. A heavy weight to carry.
You should use it to your advantage! If you worm your way up to the Freestriders using the info as leverage, you could easily land a solid gig...
Recall the instruments of this world: greed and power. Play them to your advantage as you wish. This ledger - it is nothing but another note.
Journalists. An anonymous letter. Giving it to the workers - those most affected by this corruption. That is what you must do.
Hm. Blackmail comes to mind. But really, you should probably keep it around for a while. Just in case you get fucked over during the coming power shift.
Lady Sageleaf is not the city, nor of Reedsian coin.
Out of everyone and everything, maybe she will be the one to truly make a difference with the contents of that strange, horrifying, orange ledger.
Remember, you gave it back to Viira! Good insurance for the future.
And really, what other outcome would have been preferable? Now you'll EASILY be able to worm your way into the revolutionary ranks.
You're one hell of a sneaky worm, after all...
It's in the hands of those dumb kids now. And their mysterious handler.
So who knows what kind of nefarious outcome that'll lead to?
That information is for the people now. Everyone will be hearing about it in the coming days.
But remember: you did not conjure this storm. All you did was unveil it.
Fear. That is ALL it brings.
Fear - of a CITY lost to GREED.
No matter what - YOU know the truth, from Urth himself.
The city was betrayed. You were betrayed.
Your body quakes at the slight chance - the smallest possibility of retribution against those responsible.
Time will tell.
Now get this over with, before you collect as much moss as this foul temple.
You grasp the thin card.
(Vote for The Party of Norvik.)
(Vote for The Revolutionary Freestriders.)
(Vote for The Azgalist Workers' Party.)
(Vote for The Agrarian Rural Party.)
(Vote for The Arcanist, Party of Magic.)
(Vote for The Cleric.)
(Leave it empty.)
(Fill in every box.)
You fill out the box with pride.
The last defender of humanity.
A true man.
You fill out the box for a bright future.
Free Trade. Prosperity. Democracy.
You're a revolutionary, gods be damned.
You fill out the box with a heavy heart.
For the ones who fall behind. For the ones who want to build an egalitarian dream.
You are a good person.
The box filled out. You- treading the path least traveled.
One coarse and frayed.
At last... it could lead to more APPLES.
You fill out the box with a sense of utilitarian dread.
Prax and his cabal of wizards are fools, yes. But they do represent a grand ideal.
You will easily supplant them. In time. In time.
The greatest man in the city.
The one and only hero they will ever need.
You are that hero. You are THE CLERIC.
You write in your own name at the bottom of the list.
And it is not even your full name.
But it is YOU.
You managed to spell it perfectly correct. Obviously.
The hero they need.
Wow. What an absolute <u>ego</u>.
You write in your full name at the bottom of the list.
As the ruler they need.
Your goblin companion.
Your BROTHER.
A true leader in the making.
A truly, unambiguously, wise choice.
If you vote for none of them, no one can get mad at you.
Perfect. If you vote for them all, no one can get mad at you.
You'll surely find a place in the Norvik of tomorrow.
No matter what it looks like.
(Hold up the voting card.)
<wiggle>...</wiggle>
You hold the card in your hand. The ballot box below.
A symbol for everything you are. Everything you can be. Once you put this voting card inside that box.
You have already made your choice.
Now follow the String.
XROLL-Drop the Voting Card.
The End!
